sections.heading: Overview and Scope
sections.body: This page summarizes the assessed bench strength for nine FY2026 critical roles across Operations, Finance, Technology, and Commercial functions. Roles were evaluated based on enterprise impact, revenue exposure exceeding $50M, and regulatory accountability. Bench strength ratings (Ready Now, Ready <12 Months, Ready 12–24 Months, No Identified Successor) reflect validated talent reviews conducted in November–December 2025. The analysis incorporates performance history, mobility, retention risk, and leadership potential indicators.

sections.heading: Bench Strength Snapshot
sections.body: Of the nine roles assessed, two are classified as strong (2+ Ready Now successors), four as moderate (at least one Ready <12 Months successor), and three as weak or at risk. The Chief Information Security Officer and VP, North America Manufacturing each have two Ready Now successors with cross-functional exposure. In contrast, the Controller and Head of Clinical Compliance roles have no internal candidates rated Ready Now and only one individual in each pipeline assessed as Ready 12–24 Months. Overall enterprise bench strength index improved from 1.1 to 1.4 successors per role compared to FY2025, but remains below the target of 1.8.

sections.heading: High-Potential Successor Profiles
sections.body: Identified high-potential successors include Priya Raman (Director, Financial Planning), rated Ready <12 Months for Controller contingent on external audit rotation, and Marcus LeBlanc (Sr. Director, Cyber Defense), rated Ready Now for CISO with expanded board exposure. Elena Kovács (Plant Director, Brno) is assessed as Ready <12 Months for VP, NA Manufacturing pending U.S. labor law certification. For Head of Clinical Compliance, Dr. Aaron Feld is the sole internal candidate (Ready 12–24 Months) and requires broader FDA inspection leadership experience. Retention risk is elevated for Raman and LeBlanc due to active external market approaches.

sections.heading: Development Actions and Timelines
sections.body: Time-bound development plans have been formalized with quarterly progress checkpoints. Raman will lead the FY2026 external audit engagement (Q2–Q3) and complete executive finance certification by October 2026. LeBlanc will present two cybersecurity briefings to the Audit Committee and assume interim crisis response lead during the Q4 simulation exercise. Kovács will relocate to the U.S. for a six-month operational rotation beginning July 2026, and Feld will co-lead the next FDA mock inspection cycle in September 2026.

sections.heading: Emergency Coverage and Risk Mitigation
sections.body: Emergency succession gaps are most acute for Controller and Head of Clinical Compliance, where immediate departure would require interim external placement. A contingency agreement has been initiated with Ridgeway Executive Interim Services to provide temporary financial leadership within 30 days if required. Additionally, cross-training between the Deputy Controller and Treasury Lead has been accelerated to reduce single-point-of-failure risk. A formal risk review will be presented to the Executive Committee in April 2026 to reassess mitigation effectiveness.

structure.full_text:
FY2026 Succession Bench Strength Assessment – Critical Roles
Ref: SP-26-017 | Date: 09 January 2026 | From: Talent Management Office

Section Overview and Scope
This page summarizes the assessed bench strength for nine FY2026 critical roles across Operations, Finance, Technology, and Commercial functions. Roles were evaluated based on enterprise impact, revenue exposure exceeding $50M, and regulatory accountability. Bench strength ratings (Ready Now, Ready <12 Months, Ready 12–24 Months, No Identified Successor) reflect validated talent reviews conducted in November–December 2025. The analysis incorporates performance history, mobility, retention risk, and leadership potential indicators.

Section Bench Strength Snapshot
Of the nine roles assessed, two are classified as strong (2+ Ready Now successors), four as moderate (at least one Ready <12 Months successor), and three as weak or at risk. The Chief Information Security Officer and VP, North America Manufacturing each have two Ready Now successors with cross-functional exposure. In contrast, the Controller and Head of Clinical Compliance roles have no internal candidates rated Ready Now and only one individual in each pipeline assessed as Ready 12–24 Months. Overall enterprise bench strength index improved from 1.1 to 1.4 successors per role compared to FY2025, but remains below the target of 1.8.

Section High-Potential Successor Profiles
Identified high-potential successors include Priya Raman (Director, Financial Planning), rated Ready <12 Months for Controller contingent on external audit rotation, and Marcus LeBlanc (Sr. Director, Cyber Defense), rated Ready Now for CISO with expanded board exposure. Elena Kovács (Plant Director, Brno) is assessed as Ready <12 Months for VP, NA Manufacturing pending U.S. labor law certification. For Head of Clinical Compliance, Dr. Aaron Feld is the sole internal candidate (Ready 12–24 Months) and requires broader FDA inspection leadership experience. Retention risk is elevated for Raman and LeBlanc due to active external market approaches.

Section Development Actions and Timelines
Time-bound development plans have been formalized with quarterly progress checkpoints. Raman will lead the FY2026 external audit engagement (Q2–Q3) and complete executive finance certification by October 2026. LeBlanc will present two cybersecurity briefings to the Audit Committee and assume interim crisis response lead during the Q4 simulation exercise. Kovács will relocate to the U.S. for a six-month operational rotation beginning July 2026, and Feld will co-lead the next FDA mock inspection cycle in September 2026.

Section Emergency Coverage and Risk Mitigation
Emergency succession gaps are most acute for Controller and Head of Clinical Compliance, where immediate departure would require interim external placement. A contingency agreement has been initiated with Ridgeway Executive Interim Services to provide temporary financial leadership within 30 days if required. Additionally, cross-training between the Deputy Controller and Treasury Lead has been accelerated to reduce single-point-of-failure risk. A formal risk review will be presented to the Executive Committee in April 2026 to reassess mitigation effectiveness.

structure.heading: FY2026 Critical Role Bench Strength and Emergency Coverage Assessment
text_content: **FY2026 Critical Role Bench Strength and Emergency Coverage Assessment**

2026, nine (9) critical roles are in scope for succession planning across the enterprise. These roles, reviewed by the Executive Committee, span Finance, Technology, Operations, Legal, HR, and Sales. Baseline documentation is current: 100% of roles are recorded in the succession inventory and risk-rated in Q1 FY2026.

Current bench strength is uneven: 3 of 9 critical roles (33.3%) have zero 'Ready Now (0–3 months)' successors, exposing near-term continuity risk. The other six roles include a mix of 'Ready Soon (3–12 months)' and 'Developing (>12 months)' successors. Talent & OD will target accelerated readiness, short-term assignments, and mentoring to move candidates to operational readiness.

Emergency coverage gaps persist: 2 of 9 critical roles (22.2%) have no designated emergency interim leader, increasing exposure during unplanned departures. Recommended actions by May 31, 2026 include appointing interim designees, formalizing emergency delegation protocols, and certifying interim coverage. Business Owners and Talent & OD must complete cross-training and documentation to ensure uninterrupted service and compliance, and report progress to leadership.

assertions.text: The response must state nine (9).

structure.heading: High-Potential Successor Slate and 12-Month Development Plans (FY2026)
text_content: The FY2026 HiPo slate includes 14 candidates across Director–VP levels. This slate represents cross-functional strength with candidates drawn from Enterprise Technology (4), Finance (3), Global Operations (4), and Commercial Sales (3), reflecting an 8:6 split between Director and Vice President roles (57% Director, 43% VP). Demographically, 43% of the slate are women and 29% identify as members of underrepresented ethnic groups; these figures will be tracked against the enterprise diversity goals for FY2026. Selection was based on performance history, promotability ratings, and leadership potential assessments administered by People & Culture and validated by business unit heads. The slate is intended to supply the primary successor pool for 12 identified critical roles.
